source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.section: Mutual Configurations of the Signs; sign-kind cross-reference Chapter XV
source_locator.short_quote: The opposition and quartile are considered to be discordant, because they are configurations made between signs not of the same kind

calculation_dependencies: comparison of the source's sign-kind or nature classification

condition.sign_relationship: unlike kind as stated in Chapter XVI; Chapter XV mapping unresolved

normalized_rule: Classify a quartile as discordant when it joins signs of unlike kind rather than the same masculine or feminine kind.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific sign-configuration classification, not a scientific incompatibility claim.
review_notes: The Chapter XVI discordant label is retained, but its unlike-kind condition cannot be mapped to one Chapter XV sign-gender arrangement without resolving CONFLICT-PTOLEMY-SIGN-KIND-001. No universal sign-gender scheme is selected.
transmission_notes: The label is in the Ashmand/Proclus main text. Its relationship to the Chapter XV sign-gender arrangements is unresolved; the Aries-origin sequence can produce same-gender oppositions while Chapter XVI calls opposition unlike-kind.
